title: TERRA INCOGNITA
summary: A 1914 aerial of a harbour holds until its grey water starts to read as emulsion. A 1966 earthquake film's black arc crosses a tidal flat. A decayed 1963 print of a harvester and of skaters in a park come back out of white. The film ends on a blank 1915 interval with its own noise raised.

video.card: ends with a 5 s card naming every source

searches.q: film burn, light leak end of reel
damaged emulsion, people walking through scratches
aerial view of landscape on an old damaged print
sea or shore on a badly worn film print

shots.why: recognizable: a harbor from a plane, 1914. Grain and dust are already moving but it is still a place.
same reel. The white shoreline stays and everything else becomes mottling. Held long enough that the sea starts to read as emulsion: the apparent landscape is the carrier.

following that bright edge to a different film, 1966, where a black arc crosses a tidal flat. Its narrator's Suddenly the whole harbor of Valdez is sucked dry is kept: he is describing an event, the picture is also describing its own surface.
same film, a horse and machine pulled out of white. Whatever damaged it, nobody here is shown as having chosen it.
a recognizable scene comes back through a decayed surface: skaters in a park. The pulse on the track belongs to this source.
end on a blank interval, 1915, with its own recorded noise raised: flecks and hairs and no picture.

reviews.text:
VERDICT: reference stronger (inconclusive on sound; I cannot hear it).

Noticed before the brief: 0:14 to 0:15 hard cut from a bright, blown-out aerial of water to a black-bordered shoreline with a dark arc across the right edge. The ASR line "the whole harbor of Valdez is sucked dry" at 14.4-17.6 lands on it, but the sheet shows tidal flats and not a harbor. The picture does not clearly back the words. The loudness spike at 14-16s supports a narration or sound event there.

Largest gap: the brief asks for a recognizable scene to return after a held surface, and for a visible scratch or boundary to carry the viewer between fragments. The sheet shows three fragments joined by hard cuts, at 0:15 and 0:22. At 0:40 the film goes to a near-blank gray leader that holds for about 7s. The park scene from 0:22 (sepia, blurred, then dissolving into horses and carriage at 0:34-0:39) does not return, and nothing links the shots by a defect. The 0:40-0:46 blank has no readable recorded noise on the sheet. Its transcript is repeated "I can't" at near-silence, which is probably false ASR from hiss. Nothing on the sheet shows scale or handling, and no narrator separates recollection from research. The film is 47s against a 60s brief.

Repairs:
1. At 0:15 and 0:22, add an overlap of at least 8 frames in which a scratch or vertical line from the outgoing shot stays visible in the incoming one. Check by frame-stepping.
2. At 0:40, return to the park or carriage image before the blank. The same shot should appear at both 0:22-0:33 and about 0:39. The blank should then fall after it.
3. At 0:33-0:39, the ghosted horse image reads as a generated extension. Label it as such, or cut it.

Strength to protect: the held blank leader from 0:40 to 0:46, with its dust and scratches, reads as the film's own material.
reviews.builder_note: Partly: the ghosted horse image is the source's own decayed print, and nothing in this film is generated, but the film never says so. The park and harvester shots were reordered so the park comes right before the blank interval. Scratch overlaps at the cuts were not made.

packet.note: the first cut, before any repair

repairs: Reordered so the park skaters come immediately before the blank interval.

worked: Searches for damage (scratches, nitrate decay, light leaks, countdown leaders, worn shore prints) returned many Apollo film-to-video transfers; the useful ones were two decayed 1963 'Mirror of America' prints, a 1914 aerial and a 1915 blank.
Every source keeps its own sound. The blank's hiss is raised about 20 times so it can be heard as material.
failed: The critic found no defect that carries the viewer from one fragment to the next. Cuts are hard cuts; scratch overlaps were not made.
The decayed prints read as generated to the critic. They are the sources' own damage and nothing in the film is generated, but the film says nothing about that.
open: Overlaps of at least eight frames where a scratch from the outgoing shot stays in the incoming one.
A caption saying which damage is the source's.
